title: SISTER derived constraint record
description: One record per benchmark task (see ../runs/benchmark_data.json), listing the atomic creative-writing requirements extracted from that task's full_instruction. Derived artifact — never edit runs/benchmark_data.json or runs/results/*.jsonl to produce this; regenerate from source instead.

story_id.description: domain + '_' + item_id zero-padded to 3 digits, e.g. 'fantasy_001'. item_id alone is only unique within a domain (comedy runs 1-60, all other domains 1-20), so story_id is the stable global join key against generation records via item.domain + item.item_id.

domain.description: One of: comedy, fantasy, historical_fiction, mystery, romance, science_fiction.

constraint_id.description: story_id + '_c' + running integer starting at 1, in source order.

requirement.description: Atomic requirement, paraphrased/extracted from full_instruction. Never invented beyond the source text.

introduced_at_shard.description: 0-based index into that task's shards[] array (in runs/benchmark_data.json) — the earliest shard that introduces this requirement in the sharded condition.

provenance.extraction_method: LLM extraction via Claude Code Workflow tool, 12 parallel subagent batches (~14 tasks/batch), schema-forced structured output
provenance.validation: All 160 story_ids match benchmark_data.json exactly (0 missing, 0 extra, 0 duplicates); all constraint types within taxonomy; all introduced_at_shard values within bounds of that task's shards[]; all constraint_ids unique. 1,274 total constraints, 6-12 per story (mean 8.0).
provenance.human_spot_check: 36 stories (6 randomly sampled per genre, seed=42) manually checked against full_instruction/shards on 2026-08-14. No hallucinated constraints found; no missing constraints found in the sample; introduced_at_shard mappings all correct. One systematic issue found and fixed: romance_011-020 (extraction batch 6 of 12) had bundled 'Write a short, deliberately cheesy romance story' into a single genre constraint, silently dropping the tone (cheesy) and length (short) requirements as separately-scoreable constraints, while romance_001-010 (batch 5) had correctly split them into 3. Patched romance_011-020 to match the batch-5 convention (genre/tone/length as 3 constraints); all other constraint_ids in those 10 records renumbered accordingly. Remaining 30 sampled stories (fantasy, historical_fiction, mystery, science_fiction, comedy) showed no comparable batch-boundary drift, and only romance has a domain-wide repeated compound-adjective genre phrase that was structurally vulnerable to this failure mode, so no further systematic issue is expected -- but only 36/160 stories were human-checked; treat the remaining 124 as validated only by the mechanical checks above.
